00dc50d0 <frozen os>
00dc5490 Append module search paths for third-party packages to sys.path.
00dc54d2 ****************************************************************
00dc5513 * This module is automatically imported during initialization. *
00dc5554 ****************************************************************
00dc5596 This will append site-specific paths to the module search path.  On
00dc55da Unix (including Mac OSX), it starts with sys.prefix and
00dc5612 sys.exec_prefix (if different) and appends
00dc563d lib/python<version>/site-packages.
00dc5660 On other platforms (such as Windows), it tries each of the
00dc569b prefixes directly, as well as with lib/site-packages appended.  The
00dc56df resulting directories, if they exist, are appended to sys.path, and
00dc5723 also inspected for path configuration files.
00dc5751 If a file named "pyvenv.cfg" exists one directory above sys.executable,
00dc5799 sys.prefix and sys.exec_prefix are set to that directory and
00dc57d6 it is also checked for site-packages (sys.base_prefix and
00dc5810 sys.base_exec_prefix will always be the "real" prefixes of the Python
00dc5856 installation). If "pyvenv.cfg" (a bootstrap configuration file) contains
00dc589f the key "include-system-site-packages" set to anything other than "false"
00dc58e9 (case-insensitive), the system-level prefixes will still also be
00dc592a searched for site-packages; otherwise they won't.
00dc595d All of the resulting site-specific directories, if they exist, are
00dc59a0 appended to sys.path, and also inspected for path configuration
00dc59e0 files.
00dc59e8 A path configuration file is a file whose name has the form
00dc5a24 <package>.pth; its contents are additional directories (one per line)
00dc5a6a to be added to sys.path.  Non-existing directories (or
00dc5aa1 non-directories) are never added to sys.path; no directory is added to
00dc5ae8 sys.path more than once.  Blank lines and lines beginning with
00dc5b27 '#' are skipped. Lines starting with 'import' are executed.
00dc5b64 For example, suppose sys.prefix and sys.exec_prefix are set to
00dc5ba3 /usr/local and there is a directory /usr/local/lib/python2.5/site-packages
00dc5bee with three subdirectories, foo, bar and spam, and two path
00dc5c29 configuration files, foo.pth and bar.pth.  Assume foo.pth contains the
00dc5c70 following:
00dc5c7c   # foo package configuration
00dc5c9a   foo
00dc5ca0   bar
00dc5ca6   bletch
00dc5cb0 and bar.pth contains:
00dc5cc7   # bar package configuration
00dc5ce5   bar
00dc5cec Then the following directories are added to sys.path, in this order:
00dc5d32   /usr/local/lib/python2.5/site-packages/bar
00dc5d5f   /usr/local/lib/python2.5/site-packages/foo
00dc5d8d Note that bletch is omitted because it doesn't exist; bar precedes foo
00dc5dd4 because bar.pth comes alphabetically before foo.pth; and spam is
00dc5e15 omitted because it is not mentioned in either path configuration file.
00dc5e5d The readline module is also automatically configured to enable
00dc5e9c completion for systems that support it.  This can be overridden in
00dc5edf sitecustomize, usercustomize or PYTHONSTARTUP.  Starting Python in
00dc5f22 isolated mode (-I) disables automatic readline configuration.
00dc5f61 After these operations, an attempt is made to import a module
00dc5f9f named sitecustomize, which can perform arbitrary additional
00dc5fdb site-specific customizations.  If this import fails with an
00dc6017 ImportError exception, it is silently ignored.

00dcbd78 A context manager responsible to updating ``_blocking_on``.
00dcbf30         
00dcc058 Check if 'target_id' is holding the same lock as another thread(s).
00dcc09d     The search within 'blocking_on' starts with the threads listed in
00dcc0e3     'candidate_ids'.  'seen_ids' contains any threads that are considered
00dcc12d     already traversed in the search.
00dcc153     Keyword arguments:
00dcc16a     target_id     -- The thread id to try to reach.
00dcc19e     seen_ids      -- A set of threads that have already been visited.
00dcc1e4     candidate_ids -- The thread ids from which to begin.
00dcc21d     blocking_on   -- A dict representing the thread/blocking-on graph.  This may
00dcc26e                      be the same object as the global '_blocking_on' but it is
00dcc2bd                      a parameter to reduce the impact that global mutable
00dcc307                      state has on the result of this function.

00dd04a0 The specification for a module, used for loading.
00dd04d3     A module's spec is the source for information about the module.  For
00dd051c     data associated with the module, including source, use the spec's
00dd0562     loader.
00dd056f     `name` is the absolute name of the module.  `loader` is the loader
00dd05b6     to use when loading the module.  `parent` is the name of the
00dd05f7     package the module is in.  The parent is derived from the name.
00dd063c     `is_package` determines if the module is considered a package or
00dd0681     not.  On modules this is reflected by the `__path__` attribute.
00dd06c6     `origin` is the specific location used by the loader from which to
00dd070d     load the module, if that information is available.  When filename is
00dd0756     set, origin will match.
00dd0773     `has_location` indicates that a spec's "origin" reflects a location.
00dd07bc     When this is True, `__file__` attribute of the module is set.
00dd07ff     `cached` is the location of the cached bytecode file, if any.  It
00dd0845     corresponds to the `__cached__` attribute.
00dd0875     `submodule_search_locations` is the sequence of path entries to
00dd08b9     search when importing submodules.  If set, is_package should be
00dd08fd     True--and False otherwise.
00dd091d     Packages are simply modules that (may) have submodules.  If a spec
00dd0964     has a non-None value in `submodule_search_locations`, the import
00dd09a9     system will consider modules loaded from the spec as packages.
00dd09ed     Only finders (see importlib.abc.MetaPathFinder and
00dd0a24     importlib.abc.PathEntryFinder) should modify ModuleSpec instances.
00dd0a6c

00df5658  Decodes data from the stream self.stream and returns the
00df5692             resulting object.
00df56b1             chars indicates the number of decoded code points or bytes to
00df56fb             return. read() will never return more data than requested,
00df5742             but it might return less, if there is not enough available.
00df578b             size indicates the approximate maximum number of decoded
00df57d0             bytes or code points to read for decoding. The decoder
00df5813             can modify this setting as appropriate. The default value
00df5859             -1 indicates to read and decode as much as possible.  size
00df58a0             is intended to prevent having to decode huge files in one
00df58e6             step.
00df58f9             If firstline is true, and a UnicodeDecodeError happens
00df593c             after the first line terminator in the input only the first line
00df5989             will be returned, the rest of the input will be kept until the
00df59d4             next call to read().
00df59f6             The method should use a greedy read strategy, meaning that
00df5a3d             it should read as much data as is allowed within the
00df5a7e             definition of the encoding and the given size, e.g.  if
00df5ac2             optional encoding endings or state markers are available

00df900c         Data written to the StreamRecoder is first decoded into an

00df9410  Open an encoded file using the given mode and return
00df9446         a wrapped version providing transparent encoding/decoding.
00df948a         Note: The wrapped version will only accept the object format
00df94cf         defined by the codecs, i.e. Unicode objects for most builtin
00df9514         codecs. Output is also codec dependent and will usually be
00df9557         Unicode as well.
00df9571         If encoding is not None, then the
00df959b         underlying encoded files are always opened in binary mode.
00df95de         The default file mode is 'r', meaning to open the file in read mode.
00df962c         encoding specifies the encoding which is to be used for the
00df9670         file.
00df967f         errors may be given to define the error handling. It defaults
00df96c5         to 'strict' which causes ValueErrors to be raised in case an
00df970a         encoding error occurs.
00df972a         buffering has the same meaning as for the builtin open() API.
00df9770         It defaults to -1 which means that the default buffer size will
00df97b8         be used.
00df97ca         The returned wrapped file object provides an extra attribute
00df980f         .encoding which allows querying the used encoding. This
00df984f         attribute is only available if an encoding was specified as
00df9893         parameter.
00df98a7     
00df9a90  Return a wrapped version of file which provides transparent
00df9acd         encoding translation.
00df9aec         Data written to the wrapped file is decoded according
00df9b2a         to the given data_encoding and then encoded to the underlying
00df9b70         file using file_encoding. The intermediate data type
00df9bad         will usually be Unicode but depends on the specified codecs.
00df9bf3         Bytes read from the file are decoded using file_encoding and then
00df9c3d         passed back to the caller encoded using data_encoding.
00df9c7d         If file_encoding is not given, it defaults to data_encoding.
00df9cc3         errors may be given to define the error handling. It defaults
00df9d09         to 'strict' which causes ValueErrors to be raised in case an
00df9d4e         encoding error occurs.

00e14192 +	E7
00e145c0 Directory tree generator.
00e145db     For each directory in the directory tree rooted at top (including top
00e14625     itself, but excluding '.' and '..'), yields a 3-tuple
00e14660         dirpath, dirnames, filenames
00e14686     dirpath is a string, the path to the directory.  dirnames is a list of
00e146d1     the names of the subdirectories in dirpath (including symlinks to directories,
00e14724     and excluding '.' and '..').
00e14745     filenames is a list of the names of the non-directory files in dirpath.
00e14791     Note that the names in the lists are just names, with no path components.
00e147df     To get a full path (which begins with top) to a file or directory in
00e14828     dirpath, do os.path.join(dirpath, name).
00e14856     If optional arg 'topdown' is true or not specified, the triple for a
00e1489f     directory is generated before the triples for any of its subdirectories
00e148eb     (directories are generated top down).  If topdown is false, the triple
00e14936     for a directory is generated after the triples for all of its
00e14978     subdirectories (directories are generated bottom up).
00e149b3     When topdown is true, the caller can modify the dirnames list in-place
00e149fe     (e.g., via del or slice assignment), and walk will only recurse into the
00e14a4b     subdirectories whose names remain in dirnames; this can be used to prune the
00e14a9c     search, or to impose a specific order of visiting.  Modifying dirnames when
00e14aec     topdown is false has no effect on the behavior of os.walk(), since the
00e14b37     directories in dirnames have already been generated by the time dirnames
00e14b84     itself is generated. No matter the value of topdown, the list of
00e14bc9     subdirectories is retrieved before the tuples for the directory and its
00e14c15     subdirectories are generated.
00e14c38     By default errors from the os.scandir() call are ignored.  If
00e14c7a     optional arg 'onerror' is specified, it should be a function; it
00e14cbf     will be called with one argument, an OSError instance.  It can
00e14d02     report the error to continue with the walk, or raise the exception
00e14d49     to abort the walk.  Note that the filename is available as the
00e14d8c     filename attribute of the exception object.
00e14dbd     By default, os.walk does not follow symbolic links to subdirectories on
00e14e09     systems that support them.  In order to get this functionality, set the
00e14e55     optional argument 'followlinks' to true.
00e14e83     Caution:  if you pass a relative pathname for top, don't change the
00e14ecb     current working directory between resumptions of walk.  walk never
00e14f12     changes the current directory, and assumes that the client doesn't
00e14f59     either.
00e14f66     Example:
00e14f74     import os
00e14f82     from os.path import join, getsize
00e14fa8     for root, dirs, files in os.walk('python/Lib/xml'):
00e14fe0         print(root, "consumes ")
00e15001         print(sum(getsize(join(root, name)) for name in files), end=" ")
00e1504a         print("bytes in", len(files), "non-directory files")
00e15087         if '__pycache__' in dirs:
00e150a9             dirs.remove('__pycache__')  # don't visit __pycache__ directories
00e150f8

00e156a0 Directory tree generator.
00e156bb         This behaves exactly like walk(), except that it yields a 4-tuple
00e15706             dirpath, dirnames, filenames, dirfd
00e15737         `dirpath`, `dirnames` and `filenames` are identical to walk() output,
00e15785         and `dirfd` is a file descriptor referring to the directory `dirpath`.
00e157d5         The advantage of fwalk() over walk() is that it's safe against symlink
00e15824         races (when follow_symlinks is False).
00e15854         If dir_fd is not None, it should be a file descriptor open to a directory,
00e158a7           and top should be relative; top will then be relative to that directory.
00e158fa           (dir_fd is always supported for fwalk.)
00e1592d         Caution:
00e1593e         Since fwalk() yields file descriptors, those are only valid until the
00e1598c         next iteration step, so you should dup() them if you want to keep them
00e159db         for a longer period.
00e159f9         Example:
00e15a0b         import os
00e15a1d         for root, dirs, files, rootfd in os.fwalk('python/Lib/xml'):
00e15a62             print(root, "consumes", end="")
00e15a8e             print(sum(os.stat(name, dir_fd=rootfd).st_size for name in files),
00e15add                   end="")
00e15af7             print("bytes in", len(files), "non-directory files")
00e15b38             if '__pycache__' in dirs:
00e15b5e                 dirs.remove('__pycache__')  # don't visit __pycache__ directories
